episode_title: Private Equity Software Investing with Adi Filipovic

real_qa.q: How does Resurgence Technology Partners approach value creation beyond capital deployment?
real_qa.r: Resurgence believes the holy grail is full integration between deal professionals and operators on their value creation team. They strive for coherent, predictable decision-making across all stakeholders, and have invested meaningfully in human capital capabilities, including recruiting, talent assessment, and proactively identifying talent gaps. The firm has four or five flavors of value creators: multi-time CEOs, subject matter experts in functional domains, value creation directors who quarterback full value creation plans, analytical support staff, and dedicated human capital team members focused on systems, people operations, and talent planning.
real_qa.requete: Resurgence Technology Partners value creation strategy

real_qa.q: What is Adi Filipovic's background and how did he enter private equity?
real_qa.r: Adi was born in Bosnia in the early 1980s and came to the United States as a refugee in December 1994 during the Bosnian war, eventually settling in Augusta, Georgia. He attended Furman University where he played college football as a right guard, majoring in math and economics. After college, he planned to pursue a PhD in economics but took an internship at HIG Capital in 2007 through a connection with Fred Sturgis, a Furman alumnus. He was offered a full-time position and deferred his PhD indefinitely, eventually spending 20 years at HIG before co-founding Resurgence Technology Partners with Sturgis.
real_qa.requete: Adi Filipovic background private equity career

real_qa.q: What challenges and resilience has Adi Filipovic experienced in building his private equity firm?
real_qa.r: Adi and his co-founder Fred left XL Capital to start Resurgence Technology Partners with no fund, portfolio companies, team, or pay. His first child was born at exactly that same time. During COVID, the firm had seven to eight employees and added three new team members whom they had never met in person, which caused significant concern. Currently, he describes this period as difficult and unprecedented, requiring questions about what should be done differently at every aspect of his job. He has learned to view life as a sine curve rather than a straight line, with good and bad things always happening in distribution.
real_qa.requete: Adi Filipovic Resurgence challenges resilience founding

real_qa.q: What does Adi Filipovic prioritize beyond his private equity career?
real_qa.r: Adi is on pace to attend approximately 75 live events per year, having been north of 50 events annually for a decade. These events are mostly sports, shows, or concerts, and he attends them with his eight and ten-year-old children despite the demands of his private equity job. He values the spontaneous, reactionary, and unscripted nature of live experiences, particularly following the Bosnian national football team to international games and attending NHL Predators games. He emphasizes that live events provide community, authenticity, and real human connection in contrast to the scripted and staged world of social media.
real_qa.requete: Adi Filipovic live events sports concerts attendance

real_qa.q: How large is Resurgence Technology Partners' team and portfolio?
real_qa.r: Resurgence Technology Partners has approximately 45 to 50 people total, with about half being deal professionals and half being operating professionals who have built careers operating in businesses. The firm manages 17 portfolio companies. The value creation team consists of four or five distinct flavors of professionals including multi-time CEOs, subject matter experts in functional domains, value creation directors, analytical support staff, and dedicated human capital team members.
real_qa.requete: Resurgence Technology Partners team size portfolio companies

real_qa.q: What is Adi Filipovic's philosophy on dealing with adversity and stress in private equity?
real_qa.r: Adi believes that anything good, meaningful, and fulfilling comes on the back of discomfort and hardship. However, he notes that just because something is hard does not guarantee something good will come from it. He emphasizes that life is more like a sine curve than a straight line, with good and bad things always happening. His philosophy, adopted from his football coach, is that it is never as good as it seems and never as bad as it seems, and that this too shall pass. He believes that despite having experienced hardship as a refugee, he still experiences normal stress and disappointment from professional setbacks.
real_qa.requete: Adi Filipovic adversity resilience philosophy private equity
